instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`).

Problem: study mesh refinement on a 3D cantilever block 100 x 10 x 10 mm, clamped at x = 0, with a total tip load of -100 N in y at x = 100. Build TWO decks that model the same problem:
- `/home/user/Desktop/coarse.inp`: C3D8 mesh 20 x 2 x 2 (2.5 mm along x, 5 mm across y/z; 189 nodes, 160 elements)
- `/home/user/Desktop/fine.inp`: C3D8 mesh 40 x 4 x 4 (2.5 mm cubes; 1025 nodes, 640 elements)
- node coordinates on the corresponding grids x = 0..100, y = 0..10, z = 0..10
- material E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3, one `*Solid Section` per deck
- boundary: all three dofs fixed on the whole x = 0 face
- load: -100 N total in y (dof 2) at x = 100, divided equally over the tip-face nodes; one *Cload line per node
- step: `*Static`

CalculiX allows at most 16 entries per data line; split long sets. Results reach `.dat` through `*Node Print` with an explicit node set.

Submit both jobs with `/usr/bin/ccx`, producing `coarse.dat` and `fine.dat`.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as two comma-separated numbers: `coarse_tip_uy, fine_tip_uy` — the y displacement of the node at the center of the tip face (x = 100, y = 5, z = 5) in each model, in mm.

The evaluator re-runs both decks and checks that the refined result is closer to beam theory while the two results stay consistent.
